sm: A group of comedians jokes about ancient Rome, starting with the brutality of the Colosseum, gladiator fights and the idea of a tailgate before a battle. They wonder whether people resisted the games at first, noting that emperors ran them and some disliked them. The conversation turns to Emperor Nero, who they say beat his pregnant wife to death, then castrated a slave boy named Sporus who resembled her and married him as his empress. They read that Sporus was later passed to other men, and that after Nero's death he was used in an arena reenactment of a myth, so he killed himself around the year sixty-nine. One speaker notes that history about Nero was written by people who hated him, comparing it to the story of Elizabeth Bathory, and they close with dark jokes about how bad his life was.
